chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, all from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a sacrificial animal, so it died or was stolen before he slaughtered it. He said: 'There is no problem, and if he replaces it, that is better, and if he does not buy (another one), there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / no penalty

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a sacrificial animal dies before slaughter?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the loss of a sacrificial animal before slaughter does not incur a penalty, reflecting the Shia principle that the obligation is fulfilled by the act of slaughter rather than mere possession. The Imam further notes that replacing the lost animal is superior (*afdal*), highlighting the virtue of completing the ritual perfectly even when not strictly required. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding *Udhhiyah*, distinguishing between mandatory obligations and recommended acts of worship.
